Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz delivers a smooth, tear-free experience that feels noticeably more responsive than 30 fps, while the moderate TDP keeps battery life respectable. FSR from 1024x640 produces a clean image on the Deck's 1280x800 screen.

profiles.Summary: DOOM (2016) runs excellently on the Steam Deck thanks to its highly optimised id Tech 6 engine and native Vulkan support, with ProtonDB reporting a platinum tier and strong confidence across over 1,200 reports. The Deck's RDNA 2 GPU comfortably meets and exceeds the minimum PC requirements, making smooth 60 fps achievable at medium settings.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements relative to the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class) and the game's well-known Vulkan optimisation. On first run, verify Vulkan is active in Advanced Graphics and check frame pacing in a busy combat arena before settling on a profile.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a tight 7 W TDP keeps the Deck very cool and extends battery life significantly. Vulkan must be set manually in Advanced Graphics for best efficiency.

KnownIssues: The game may default to OpenGL on first launch — manually switch to Vulkan in Advanced Graphics settings for significantly better performance and lower CPU overhead.
First-run shader compilation can cause brief stuttering; subsequent sessions are noticeably smoother.
Multiplayer and SnapMap require a broadband internet connection and Steam activation, limiting handheld offline use.
Some reports note the game defaulting to a low audio volume or incorrect audio device on first launch via Proton — check audio settings before playing.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At native 1280x800 with high settings and Vulkan, the Deck sustains near-60 fps through most of the campaign, though the most intense arena fights may dip to the low 50s. Battery life is short at full TDP — best used plugged in or for shorter sessions.

Optimal.Notes: Rendering at 1024x640 with FSR sharpened to native 1280x800 delivers a clean, fast image; Medium shadows and SSAO preserve visual fidelity without taxing the GPU. This is the sweet spot where DOOM's fast-paced combat feels fluid and the battery remains reasonable.

profiles.Summary: DOOM (2016) runs well on the Steam Deck, benefiting from id Software's highly optimized Vulkan renderer and relatively modest PC requirements that the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU can comfortably handle. The game is Steam Deck Verified and ProtonDB reporters rate it platinum, making it one of the smoother experiences on the device.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements, the Deck's GPU class (roughly GTX 1050 Ti), and DOOM's reputation for an exceptionally well-optimised Vulkan renderer. On first run, check the frame counter in a busy combat arena — if the Optimal profile dips below 55 fps, lower Shadow Quality to Low and reduce the render resolution to 960x600.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 keeps the GPU load light; the 7 W TDP cap and 900 MHz GPU clock ensure cool, quiet, long-session play. DOOM's Vulkan renderer is efficient enough that even Low settings look respectable in motion.

KnownIssues: Multiplayer and SnapMap require a broadband internet connection and may have additional compatibility considerations under Proton.
Some users report occasional stutters during the first run while shaders compile.
The game's launcher/settings menu may require mouse input on first launch before controller takes over fully.
HDR is not natively supported under Proton on SteamOS.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At native 1280x800 with High/Ultra settings DOOM's optimized Vulkan renderer can push the OLED panel's 90 Hz cap in most areas, though very dense combat encounters may dip toward 70 fps. TDP is left uncapped to let the APU boost freely; expect the fan to spin up and battery life to be short.
